summary: The document is a non-functional placeholder consisting of seven vague, subjective statements regarding a food delivery mobile app. It lacks all technical specifications, architectural definitions, user roles, data models, and security protocols. The document explicitly acknowledges its own deficiencies in a 'Major Problems' section, rendering it unusable for engineering, testing, or compliance purposes.

risk_factors.title: Total Absence of Security Architecture
risk_factors.description: The document contains zero security requirements. For a food delivery app handling PII (names, addresses) and financial data (payment info), the lack of specified authentication, encryption, or data protection mechanisms creates immediate exposure to OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define a comprehensive security architecture including OAuth2.0/OIDC for authentication, AES-256 for data at rest, TLS 1.3 for data in transit, and specific controls for PCI-DSS compliance regarding payment processing.

risk_factors.title: Undefined Data Privacy and Compliance Framework
risk_factors.description: No mention of GDPR, CCPA, or HIPAA (if health data is involved) compliance. The requirement 'Customers can pay somehow' implies financial data handling without specifying data retention, consent, or right-to-erasure mechanisms.
risk_factors.mitigation: Implement a Data Privacy Impact Assessment (DPIA). Specify data minimization principles, explicit consent flows for location tracking, and automated data deletion workflows for user accounts.

risk_factors.title: Unmeasurable Performance and SLA Requirements
risk_factors.description: Requirement #3 states 'Delivery should happen fast' and #2 states 'Food ordering must be easy'. These are subjective and untestable. Without defined latency thresholds (e.g., API response < 200ms) or delivery time windows, the system cannot be validated against business goals.
risk_factors.mitigation: Define specific Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs): API p95 latency < 300ms, app startup time < 2 seconds, and delivery ETA accuracy within +/- 5 minutes.

risk_factors.title: Ambiguous Payment Integration Scope
risk_factors.description: Requirement #4 'Customers can pay somehow' does not specify payment gateways (Stripe, PayPal, etc.), supported currencies, refund policies, or fraud detection mechanisms. This creates a critical gap in the financial transaction flow.
risk_factors.mitigation: Specify the primary payment processor, supported payment methods (Credit/Debit, Wallets), idempotency keys for transaction safety, and integration with fraud detection services.

conflicts_and_ambiguities.context: 1. The app should be awesome. 2. Food ordering must be easy.
conflicts_and_ambiguities.suggested_resolution: Replace with measurable UX metrics: 'Order completion flow must not exceed 5 taps from launch to checkout' and 'App Store rating target > 4.5 stars within 6 months of launch'.

Define specific roles: 'Restaurant Admin' (menu management, order acceptance), 'Restaurant Staff' (order status updates), 'Customer' (ordering, tracking), and 'Dispatcher' (route optimization). Map permissions to each role.
Specify notification types: Push (order confirmed, driver en route, delivered), SMS (backup), and In-App. Define trigger events and frequency limits to prevent spam.
Define minimum viable reporting for launch: Daily sales summary, Order status breakdown, and Customer feedback aggregation. Specify data retention period for report generation.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: The core business logic of placing, tracking, and completing an order is entirely absent. Without this, no backend services or frontend flows can be designed.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Detailed state machine for orders: Created -> Confirmed -> Preparing -> Out for Delivery -> Delivered -> Completed. Include edge cases: Cancellation, Refund, Delivery Failure.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No performance, availability, scalability, or reliability targets are defined. This makes capacity planning and infrastructure selection impossible.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Specify: 99.9% uptime SLA, support for 10,000 concurrent users, API response time < 500ms, mobile app compatibility (iOS 15+, Android 10+).

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No definition of core entities (User, Restaurant, Menu Item, Order, Payment, Driver). This prevents database schema design and API contract definition.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Provide an ERD or JSON schema for key entities. Define relationships: User places Order, Order contains Menu Items, Order linked to Payment, Order assigned to Driver.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No specification for user login, session management, or data protection. This is a critical gap for any app handling PII and financial data.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: Specify: JWT-based authentication, password hashing (bcrypt), MFA for admin roles, encryption of PII fields, and secure storage of API keys.

missing_sections_and_details.why_missing: No mention of third-party services (Maps, Payments, SMS/Push). This creates ambiguity in external dependencies and cost estimation.
missing_sections_and_details.recommended_addition: List required integrations: Google Maps/Mapbox for geolocation, Stripe/PayPal for payments, Twilio/Firebase for notifications. Define API contracts for each.

ai_recommendations: Discard the current document and initiate a formal requirements elicitation workshop with stakeholders (Product, Engineering, Security, Legal) to define specific, testable functional and non-functional requirements.
Adopt a standard requirements framework (e.g., IEEE 830 or Agile User Stories with Acceptance Criteria) to ensure all requirements are SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound).

Immediately engage a Security Architect to define the threat model and security controls for the food delivery domain, focusing on PII protection, payment security (PCI-DSS), and location data privacy (GDPR/CCPA).
Define the core data model and API contracts before proceeding to UI/UX design to ensure technical feasibility and alignment between frontend and backend teams.
